column3: The Hebrew says the LORD answered Job and spoke; BSB says He said to Job.
The Hebrew says he has placed his hand at his mouth; BSB uses I place.
The Hebrew says he will not answer; BSB says he has no answer.
The Hebrew explicitly says to gird his loins; BSB says brace yourself.
The Hebrew says to bind their faces in a hidden place; BSB describes imprisoning them in the grave.
The Hebrew uses a verb of praising or acknowledging and says his right hand saves him; BSB describes confessing that it can save him.
The Hebrew describes stiffening his tail; BSB says it sways.
The Hebrew names the beginning of God’s ways and does not separately express only; BSB says foremost works and only his Maker.
The Hebrew has mountains and says the animals play there; BSB has hills and nearby.
The Hebrew has snares in the plural; BSB has a snare.
